Definition: from the same as G712 and G757; best ruling; Aristarchus, a Macedonian:--Aristarchus.
BiblicalUsage: Aristarchus is the Macedonian who stays with Paul through the worst of it. He is seized in the riot at Ephesus, sails with Paul as a prisoner to Rome, and is still beside him in prison when Paul writes to the Colossians, calling him a fellow prisoner.
TheologicalSignificance: A man named three times for staying put is worth noticing, because faithfulness is mostly that: being there when it costs something, and still being there years later.
